lastRun.summary: The desk maintains its active 20-day short Brent position (wt13za) to capture the historical post-escalation premium decay, which represents the only walk-forward validated statistical edge in our event study. Given that fresh tanker attacks and mine strikes carry no out-of-sample persistence for momentum trades in crude or tanker equities, we refrain from adding new gross exposure. We preserve existing risk limits while monitoring diplomatic messaging and US naval blockade developments around the Persian Gulf.
lastRun.noTrade: The desk already holds exposure to the 20-day post-escalation fade via active paper trade wt13za. Out-of-sample walk-forward testing demonstrates that short-term 1-day and 5-day directional momentum following maritime attacks in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz lacks statistical edge across crude outrights and shipping equities (FRO 5d p-value 0.910; Brent 1d p-value 0.910). Adding further positions under active mine-strike headlines would introduce uncompensated volatility.

backtest.method: Same prompt, schema, maths and risk checks as the live desk. Point-in-time inputs only. Entry at the first daily close after the news; stops/targets checked on daily closes; round-trip costs charged. Book P&L = R x risk% of book.
backtest.caveat: The model may already know how these events played out from its training data, which would flatter these results. Treat this as a test of the machinery and of calibration; the live paper record is the only truly unseen test.
